title: Identifiability of students and parents through account records
description: The grading service writes account records to the directory, likely including direct identifiers or uniquely identifying attributes. Combining those records with parent-child links can make both children and guardians readily identifiable, even where another subsystem might otherwise only need pseudonymous references.
assumptions: Account records contain names, usernames, email addresses, student numbers, guardian details, or other unique attributes.
uncertainty_note: Exact identifying fields are not listed in the flow description, but identifiability is a genuine risk for account-directory writes.

title: Insufficient proof of who created or changed directory relationships
description: If the grading service writes account records and parent-child links without strong auditability, the service or its operators may later be unable to prove which relationship entries were created, modified, or deleted. This can undermine accountability for privacy-relevant changes affecting minors and guardians.
assumptions: Write operations to the directory may lack tamper-evident logs, actor attribution, or retained change history.
uncertainty_note: Applies if audit trails for directory writes are weak; the flow description does not confirm logging controls.

title: Detectability of family relationships from directory updates or queries
description: The existence of writes for parent-child relationship links may allow an observer with access to directory traffic, metadata, or change notifications to detect that a specific student has an associated guardian account or that a family relationship was created or changed, even without seeing full record contents.
assumptions: Some actors can observe directory access patterns, metadata, synchronization events, or partial contents.
uncertainty_note: Threat depends on visibility of metadata or update events; not all architectures expose this.

title: Disclosure of sensitive relationship and account data in the directory
description: The account directory becomes a repository of account records and parent-child links. Unauthorized access, overbroad internal access, or insecure storage could disclose personal data about students and guardians, including the fact of their relationship.
assumptions: The directory stores personal data and relationship links in readable form and may be accessible by multiple services or administrators.
uncertainty_note: None

title: Unawareness of directory storage and reuse of parent-child links
description: Students and parents may be unaware that the grading service writes their account records and family relationship links into a shared account directory, potentially for reuse by other services, administrators, or downstream processes. This reduces transparency about where relationship data is stored and how long it is retained.
assumptions: The system does not clearly inform users about this directory write, downstream reuse, or retention of relationship data.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the presence and quality of privacy notices and user-facing explanations.

title: Non-compliant storage of minors' and guardians' relationship data
description: Persisting account records together with parent-child relationship links in the directory may violate data-minimization, purpose-limitation, retention, or child-data protection requirements if more data than necessary is stored, reused beyond grading/account purposes, or retained too long.
assumptions: The directory may be shared across services, retain data beyond necessity, or lack a clearly defined lawful basis and retention policy for family-link data.
uncertainty_note: Compliance impact depends on jurisdiction, age of users, and actual governance controls, but the flow clearly raises child/guardian privacy compliance concerns.

title: Excessive disclosure of student and staff personal data to third-party cloud host
description: The nightly backup/replication sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to an external cloud hosting provider. This is an intentional transfer of personal data across a trust boundary and may disclose more data than is strictly necessary for backup/hosting purposes, violating data minimization.
assumptions: The cloud hosting provider is a separate third party and receives or can access the replicated backup contents in identifiable form.
uncertainty_note: Tree node id is best-judgement for explicit third-party disclosure/minimization; retrieved context confirms Dd applicability to Process→ExternalEntity but does not provide the exact subtree id.

title: Replicated full records enable identification of individuals by the cloud provider
description: Because the transfer includes full grade records, assignments, and an account directory, the recipient can directly identify students and staff. If identification is not necessary for the hosting task, the flow creates an avoidable identifiability threat.
assumptions: Transferred data contains direct identifiers or stable account identifiers linked to individuals.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-judgement; identifiability is strongly implied by 'full grade records' and 'account directory'.

title: Comprehensive backup replication enables linkage across academic and account datasets
description: Combining grade records, assignment data, and the account directory in one replicated dataset allows the cloud provider or anyone with access there to link academic performance, coursework, and account information for the same individuals. This aggregation increases the ability to correlate data across contexts.
assumptions: The replicated datasets share common identifiers or can otherwise be correlated.
uncertainty_note: Exact subtree id is best-judgement; linkage risk is grounded in the combined transfer of multiple related datasets.

title: Third-party backup transfer may be incompatible with user expectations or legal basis
description: Sending full educational records and account-directory data to a third-party cloud host may exceed the purposes users were informed about, or may require additional contractual, jurisdictional, or regulatory safeguards. If the disclosure is not transparently communicated and justified, the flow creates a non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Educational records and account data are subject to privacy obligations and may require purpose limitation, transparency, and processor controls.
uncertainty_note: Non-compliance depends on actual notices, contracts, jurisdictions, and safeguards, which are not provided.

title: Linkability of grade records across audiences
description: The grading service reads the same grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views. If identifiers or stable pseudonyms are reused across these views, the service can link records and interactions for the same student across contexts, enabling correlation beyond what each audience needs to know.
assumptions: P2 prepares distinct role-based views from a common underlying grade record set and may reuse common identifiers across them.
uncertainty_note: Tree node is best-judgement because the retrieved context only gives applicable threat types, not detailed node mappings.

title: Identifiability of students from retrieved grade records
description: When P2 reads grade records to generate views, the data likely contains direct identifiers or combinations of attributes that identify individual students. This makes students identifiable to recipients of the views and to internal operators of the service beyond strictly necessary processing.
assumptions: Grade records include names, student IDs, class/course context, or other attributes sufficient to identify a student.
uncertainty_note: Detailed threat-tree node id is approximate.

title: Excessive disclosure of grade information in generated views
description: A single read path from the grade records database is used to build student, parent, and teacher views. If role-based filtering is incomplete, P2 may disclose more grade details, historical records, comments, or records about other students than necessary for the intended audience.
assumptions: Different audiences are entitled to different subsets of grade data, and P2 enforces those distinctions when constructing views.
uncertainty_note: Threat is grounded in the described multi-audience use of the same records; node id is approximate.

title: Unawareness of secondary use of grade records
description: Students and possibly parents may be unaware that the grading service reads stored grade records not only for teacher administration but also to construct multiple audience-specific views. Without clear notice, data subjects may not understand who can access which grade details and for what purposes.
assumptions: The system does not fully communicate these read operations, audiences, retention, or purpose distinctions to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Applies if transparency notices are incomplete; exact tree node is approximate.

title: Use of grade records beyond consent or authorization expectations
description: Reading grade records to build parent, student, and teacher views may exceed the scope originally communicated or authorized if consent, school policy, or legal basis does not clearly cover each audience and purpose. This creates a risk that processing is not compliant with applicable privacy requirements.
assumptions: Different legal bases, consent states, or policy constraints may apply to student, parent, and teacher access to grade information.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the institution's legal basis and policy design; node id is approximate.
